entries.name: Temasek Foundation - NUS Leadership Enrichment and Regional Networking (TF-NUS LEaRN) Programme
entries.provider: Temasek Foundation with National University of Singapore
entries.fields: any (leadership, community engagement and ASEAN networking for undergraduates)
covers: S$1,500 award toward return airfare and living expenses
entries.eligibility: Full-time undergraduates at partner universities in Southeast Asia/ASEAN, nominated by their home university; good English and interest in leadership and community work; roughly two-week residential programme at NUS in July.
entries.cambodia_note: Application is by university nomination only: Cambodian students should ask their university's international office whether it is a TF-NUS LEaRN partner. Similar TF LEaRN programmes run with NTU and SMU.
entries.deadline_note: Partner-university nomination deadline is around mid-March each year for the July programme.

entries.name: Eisenhower Fellowships Global Program
entries.provider: Eisenhower Fellowships (foundation)
entries.fields: any (mid-career leaders from business, government, civil society, academia)
entries.eligibility: Accomplished mid-career leaders (typically in their 30s to mid-40s) with a track record of leadership and impact, citizenship of or at least five years' residence in the country represented, fluent English, and availability for the roughly six-week program (early April to mid-May 2027 for the 2027 cohort).
entries.cambodia_note: Applications are welcomed worldwide, so Cambodians can apply online; candidates from countries with an active Eisenhower Fellowships network are prioritised. 2027 Global Program applications closed in May 2026.
entries.deadline_note: Opens around April and closes mid-May each year for the following spring's program.

entries.name: Hansen Leadership Institute
entries.provider: Hansen Leadership Institute, University of San Diego (Fred J. Hansen Foundation)
entries.fields: any (leadership, conflict resolution, cross-cultural cooperation)
entries.eligibility: University students and recent graduates aged 20-25 at the start of the program, from any country, with strong English and demonstrated leadership; three-week summer institute at the University of San Diego, California.
entries.cambodia_note: Open to all nationalities; Cambodians apply online directly. International applicants have an earlier deadline (15 January 2026 for the 2026 institute).
entries.deadline_note: Applications open in autumn; international deadline is mid-January, U.S. deadline mid-March, for the July program.

entries.name: kanthari Institute for Social Leadership - Social Change Makers Course
entries.provider: kanthari (non-profit institute), Trivandrum, Kerala, India
entries.fields: Social entrepreneurship and founding of social-change organisations
entries.eligibility: Aged 22 or over with no upper age limit, from any country, who have overcome adversity or witnessed a social problem and have a concrete plan to start a social initiative; working English; residential course beginning in April each year.
entries.cambodia_note: Open worldwide, so Cambodian applicants apply directly online; kanthari has hosted participants from Southeast Asia.
entries.deadline_note: Applications usually close in January for the course starting in April of the same year.

entries.name: Asia Foundation Development Fellows
entries.provider: The Asia Foundation
entries.fields: Governance, economic development, women's empowerment, environmental resilience, education and leadership, international cooperation
covers: program costs for U.S. and Asia (Korea) leadership modules
entries.eligibility: Citizens or residents of eligible Asia-Pacific countries including Cambodia, under 40 years old on 1 January of the fellowship year, conversant in English (no TOEFL required), able to obtain a U.S. visa, with a demonstrable record of leadership in the Foundation's fields of expertise.
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is an eligible country (The Asia Foundation has a Cambodia office); Cambodians apply online directly.
entries.deadline_note: Call published around late September/October with a deadline in November for the following year's cohort.

entries.name: Korea Foundation Fellowship for Korean Language Training
entries.provider: The Korea Foundation (Government of the Republic of Korea)
entries.fields: Korean language (for Korean studies students, researchers and Korea-related professionals)
entries.eligibility: Undergraduates from Southeast Asia (and other listed regions) majoring or minoring in Korean studies/Korean language, master's or doctoral candidates in Korea-related fields with a research plan, university lecturers and researchers in Korea-related fields, and arts and culture professionals; must already speak at least basic Korean. Six to twelve months at a Korean university language institute.
entries.cambodia_note: Southeast Asia is explicitly listed for undergraduate eligibility, so Cambodian students of Korean language (e.g., at RUPP) can apply online via the KF Application Portal.
entries.deadline_note: Announced annually on the KF Application Portal, usually in the second half of the year for the following year's intake.

entries.name: ASEAN-Korea Youth Network Workshop
entries.provider: ASEAN-Korea Centre (intergovernmental organisation, Seoul)
entries.fields: ASEAN-Korea cooperation, youth networking and thematic workshops
entries.eligibility: Young people (students and young professionals) who are nationals of an ASEAN member state, with good English; about 20 participants selected from the ten ASEAN countries.
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly by emailing the application to youth@aseankorea.org during the call period.
entries.deadline_note: 2026 call ran 18 March to 8 April 2026; similar spring window expected in 2027.

entries.name: Millennium Fellowship
entries.provider: United Nations Academic Impact and Millennium Campus Network
entries.fields: any (student-led social impact projects aligned with the SDGs)
covers: free semester-long leadership training on the student's own campus
entries.eligibility: Undergraduate students aged 18 or over enrolled at a college or university anywhere in the world; applicants apply as part of a campus cohort and must commit to a semester of leadership sessions and a social-impact project.
entries.cambodia_note: Open worldwide, so students at Cambodian universities can apply online; the program runs on the student's home campus, not abroad.
entries.deadline_note: Applications for the Class of 2026 closed 28 February 2026; the Class of 2027 application is announced as opening shortly, with a similar early-year deadline expected.

entries.name: Erasmus+ International Credit Mobility (KA171)
entries.provider: European Union (Erasmus+ programme), via European universities and their Cambodian partner universities
entries.fields: any (depends on the inter-institutional agreement between the Cambodian and European university)
entries.eligibility: Students enrolled at a Cambodian university that holds an Erasmus+ KA171 agreement with a European partner; mobility of 2-12 months for study or traineeship, with language level set by the host university (often English B2).
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is an eligible partner country; students cannot apply to the EU directly but through their home university's international office (e.g., Institute of Technology of Cambodia with Université de Toulouse, Royal University of Phnom Penh with various EU partners) when the partner university issues a call.
entries.deadline_note: Each European university issues its own calls; many run in spring for the following autumn and in autumn for the spring semester.
entries.language_req: Set by host university, typically English B2

entries.name: AAUW International Fellowships
entries.provider: American Association of University Women (AAUW), US non-profit
entries.fields: Priority for STEM disciplines; any field accepted for master's/doctoral study in the US
covers: Cash fellowship stipend (roughly US$20,000 master's, US$25,000 doctoral, US$50,000 postdoctoral) paid to the fellow
entries.eligibility: Identify as a woman; not a US citizen or permanent resident; hold a degree equivalent to a US bachelor's with minimum cumulative GPA 3.5/4.0; admitted or enrolled in first master's or doctoral program (or postdoctoral research) at an accredited US institution; program must begin on or before 15 Sept 2027 and end after 30 April 2028; commitment to return home / serve women and girls
entries.cambodia_note: Open to women of any non-US nationality; Cambodian women apply directly online, no embassy or MoEYS involvement
entries.deadline_note: Applications open in August and close mid-November each year (15 November in recent cycles); results in April
entries.language_req: English proficiency required (TOEFL/IELTS or waiver if degree taught in English)

entries.name: Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG) - US/Canada Program
entries.provider: Margaret McNamara Education Grants (World Bank family charity)
entries.fields: Any field, with a demonstrated commitment to improving the lives of women and children in developing countries
covers: One-time grant of about US$15,000 towards tuition and living costs
entries.eligibility: Self-identifying woman from an eligible developing country (World Bank low/lower-middle income list); at least 25 years old; already enrolled in an in-person program at an accredited university in the US or Canada (separate programs exist for France, South Africa and Latin America); intends to return to work in a developing country; not related to World Bank Group staff
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is a lower-middle-income country and therefore on MMEG's eligibility country list; Cambodian women already enrolled at a US or Canadian university apply online
entries.deadline_note: US-Canada program accepts applications 15 September to 15 January each year; France program 15 October to 15 January

entries.name: P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship (IPS)
entries.provider: P.E.O. Sisterhood (US women's philanthropic organisation)
entries.fields: Any graduate field
covers: Scholarship of up to US$12,500 per academic year towards tuition and living costs
entries.eligibility: Woman who is not a US or Canadian citizen/permanent resident; admitted to full-time graduate study at an accredited institution in the US or Canada; has a full year of coursework remaining; intends to return to her home country after study; must first submit an Eligibility Form
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian women are eligible; apply online directly to P.E.O. (no embassy or government nomination)
entries.deadline_note: Eligibility forms accepted from about 15 September to 15 December; completed applications due 1 February (already enrolled) or 15 March (not yet enrolled); awards announced in May

entries.name: Zonta International Amelia Earhart Fellowship
entries.provider: Zonta International / Zonta Foundation for Women
entries.fields: Aerospace engineering and space sciences (PhD research)
covers: US$12,000 fellowship, usable at any accredited university worldwide
entries.eligibility: Women of any nationality registered full-time in a PhD/doctoral program in aerospace-applied sciences or engineering; must have completed at least one year of the doctoral program or hold a master's in an aerospace-applied field; must not graduate before April 2028; post-docs and Zonta members not eligible
entries.cambodia_note: Open to women of any nationality; Cambodian women apply directly online
entries.deadline_note: Applications open around August and close 15 November each year; fellows announced in April

entries.name: Schlumberger Foundation Faculty for the Future Fellowship
entries.provider: Schlumberger Foundation (SLB corporate foundation)
entries.fields: STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) PhD or post-doctoral research
covers: Grant up to US$50,000 per year (PhD) or US$40,000 (post-doc), renewable, for tuition, living and research costs
entries.eligibility: Woman and citizen of an eligible developing or emerging country where women are under-represented in STEM; no dual citizenship of a developed country; enrolled, admitted or applied to a PhD or post-doctoral program at a university abroad; excellent academic record; commitment to return home to teach/research; must demonstrate leadership and outreach
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is on the Foundation's eligible country list; Cambodian women apply directly through the online portal
entries.deadline_note: Applications open in September and close early November each year (7 November 2026, noon CST, for 2027 awards)

entries.name: OWSD PhD Fellowships for Women Scientists from Science- and Technology-Lagging Countries
entries.provider: Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World (OWSD) / Sida
entries.fields: Natural, engineering and information technology sciences
entries.eligibility: Woman scientist from one of the eligible least-developed/S&T-lagging countries; master's degree in a science field; full-time or sandwich PhD at a host institute in another developing country (Global South); maximum age 40 at application in past calls; must not reside in a developed country
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia (a UN Least Developed Country) is on OWSD's eligible country list; apply online. OWSD held no PhD call in 2025 and the next call date has not been announced, so check the site
entries.deadline_note: Historically the call opened in October/November and closed in March/April; no call was issued in 2025 and the next call is not yet scheduled
entries.language_req: English proficiency required by host institute

entries.name: ASEAN-UK SAGE Women in STEM Scholarships (British Council)
entries.provider: UK FCDO / UK Mission to ASEAN, delivered by the British Council
entries.fields: STEM master's courses at partner UK universities (Cranfield University and University of Stirling)
entries.eligibility: Women who are citizens and residents of an ASEAN member state (including Cambodia) or Timor-Leste; undergraduate degree qualifying for the chosen master's; demonstrated need for financial support; intend to return to home country; not previously funded by a UK government scholarship
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is explicitly listed as eligible; apply directly to the partner UK university's scholarship page (see British Council Cambodia page for links)
entries.deadline_note: Applications usually open in January/February and close in March/April each year for study starting the following September; the 2026-27 round has closed
entries.language_req: IELTS 6.5 or equivalent (pre-sessional English support available)

entries.name: Generation Google Scholarship (APAC)
entries.provider: Google
entries.fields: Computer science, computer engineering or closely related technical field
covers: One-off award of US$2,500 towards tuition/education expenses
invitation to a Google scholars retreat
invitation to a virtual Google scholars' retreat
entries.eligibility: Students who identify as women (or who are otherwise under-represented in tech) enrolled full-time at a university in the Asia-Pacific region for the coming academic year; strong academic record; demonstrated leadership and passion for computer science
entries.cambodia_note: Open to students at universities anywhere in Asia-Pacific, which includes Cambodia; apply directly online to Google
entries.deadline_note: Usually opens around November/December and closes in January/February; check the page as dates shift year to year

entries.name: Schwarzman Scholars
entries.provider: Schwarzman Scholars / Tsinghua University (Stephen A. Schwarzman)
entries.fields: One-year Master of Global Affairs at Schwarzman College, Tsinghua University, Beijing
entries.eligibility: Undergraduate degree conferred by 1 August of enrollment year; aged 18 to under 29 on 1 August of enrollment year; any nationality; strong English proficiency (test scores unless studied in English for 2+ years); leadership potential
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply through the Global application (no embassy or government nomination); interviews are held regionally
entries.deadline_note: Global application opens in April and closes in early-to-mid September each year (9 September 2026 for the 2027-28 cohort); the next cycle closes September 2027
entries.language_req: TOEFL 100 / IELTS 7.0 or waiver for English-medium degree

entries.name: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
entries.provider: Gates Cambridge Trust (Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation endowment), University of Cambridge
entries.fields: Any full-time postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge (PhD, MPhil, one-year master's)
covers: discretionary academic development and family allowances
entries.eligibility: Citizen of any country outside the UK; applying for a full-time postgraduate residential course at Cambridge; selected on academic excellence, reasons for choice of course, leadership and commitment to improving the lives of others
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians are in the international round; apply via the Cambridge Graduate Application Portal and tick the Gates Cambridge funding box
entries.deadline_note: Opens early September; international applicants must apply by 4 December or the earlier course deadline; interviews in March

entries.name: Global Rhodes Scholarships
entries.provider: Rhodes Trust, University of Oxford
entries.fields: Any full-time postgraduate degree at the University of Oxford
entries.eligibility: Citizens of countries with no Rhodes constituency (Cambodia qualifies); aged 18 to 23 on 1 October of the year of application (up to 26 if first degree completed late); bachelor's degree with first-class or equivalent GPA; must be nominated by the university where the first degree was obtained; only two Global Scholarships per year
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia has no national Rhodes constituency, so Cambodians apply to the Global Rhodes Scholarships and must secure a nomination from their undergraduate university
entries.deadline_note: Applications open in June; university nomination and application close around late July / early August each year for study the following October

entries.name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
entries.provider: Stanford University (Knight-Hennessy Scholars program)
entries.fields: Any full-time Stanford graduate degree (MA, MS, MBA, JD, MD, PhD, etc.)
entries.eligibility: Citizens and residents of all countries; must earn first bachelor's degree in January 2020 or later (2027 cohort); must separately apply to and be admitted by a Stanford graduate program; no age or field restrictions
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly online; a separate Stanford graduate program application must also be submitted (by 1 December 2026 if the program deadline is later)
entries.deadline_note: Application opens in early summer and closes in early October each year (6 October 2026, 1 pm Pacific, for the 2027 cohort)

entries.name: Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship
entries.provider: Peking University (Yenching Academy)
entries.fields: Interdisciplinary Master's in China Studies (economics and management, history and archaeology, law and society, literature and culture, philosophy and religion, politics and international relations)
entries.eligibility: Bachelor's degree obtained by August of enrollment year; typically aged under about 27 at enrollment; strong academic record; international applicants apply directly; English-language program (no Chinese required)
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply online directly to the Academy (international applicant track); interviews are conducted online or regionally
entries.deadline_note: Applications for international candidates usually open in September and close in early December each year for enrollment the following September
entries.language_req: English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS unless degree taught in English)
